stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The bluestreak cleaner wrasse spends its days picking parasites off larger reef fish. Because of this, marine biologists long assumed that the wrasse's clients put up with it purely for that service. ______, a field study led by marine biologist Tomasz Rehak found that client fish kept visiting cleaning stations just as often after divers had already removed all of their parasites. The finding suggests that the fish seek out the wrasse's touch for its own sake.
explanation: The first part sets up a long-held assumption: clients tolerate the wrasse only because it removes parasites. The study then shows that clients keep coming even when there are no parasites left to remove, which undercuts that assumption. A sentence that overturns an expectation needs a contrast word, and 'However' is the only contrast word among the choices.

A.why: You saw that both sentences are about why clients visit the wrasse and never checked which way the logic runs. The assumption doesn't cause the study's result. The result goes against it.

B.why: 'Similarly' says the second sentence matches the first. The study contradicts the assumption instead of repeating it.

D.why: 'For instance' would make the study one example of the belief that clients come only for parasite removal. The study is evidence against that belief, not an example of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Seismologist Priya Anand's network of low-cost sensors in the Andes has mapped hundreds of previously unknown faults, sharpened regional hazard maps, and trained dozens of local technicians to maintain the equipment. ______, Anand ranks none of these above a single episode: in 2021 the sensors picked up slow slip beneath a valley town weeks before a magnitude 5.8 earthquake, which gave officials time to reinforce two schools.
explanation: The first sentence lists the network's big achievements, so you'd expect Anand to be proudest of those. The next sentence turns against the list: she values one early warning more than all of them. That pivot away from the list calls for a concession, and 'Still' is the only one offered.

B.why: This is the list-of-successes trap. The early warning sounds like one more achievement, so you picked an addition word. But the sentence doesn't add to the list. It ranks one event above everything on it, and that is a turn away from the list.

C.why: Mapping faults and training technicians didn't cause Anand to value the 2021 warning more. 'As a result' claims a cause-and-effect link that the passage never states.

D.why: The 2021 warning isn't one of the listed achievements (faults, hazard maps, technicians). The sentence sets it apart from them, so it can't be an example of them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Standard labor-market models predict that a sharp minimum-wage increase will shrink teenage employment, since teenagers are usually the least experienced workers on a payroll. Economist Ruth Okafor expected to see exactly that pattern when she tracked teen employment for three years after the province of Velmar raised its minimum wage by 18 percent. ______, the decline never appeared: teen employment held steady, and employers reported spending less on recruiting replacements for workers who quit.
explanation: The text sets up a clear expectation: the models, and Okafor herself, predicted a drop in teen jobs. The next sentence reports that the drop never happened. A result that goes against a stated expectation needs a contrast word, so 'However' is correct.

A.why: 'Accordingly' means the next sentence follows from the one before. Okafor's expectation of a decline can't lead to finding no decline. That result goes against the expectation.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces a restatement. The sentence after the blank says the opposite of what Okafor expected, so it doesn't restate anything.

D.why: Both sentences are about teen employment, so you treated them as going in the same direction. 'Likewise' signals agreement, but the finding contradicts the prediction.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Agronomist Lena Vogt's advice to wheat growers in drought-prone regions was straightforward: irrigate lightly and often so that seedlings never wilt. To test it, farmer Dario Mendez followed Vogt's schedule on half of his fields and watered the other half only twice all season. ______, it was the sparsely watered wheat that produced more grain. Deprived of surface moisture, its roots had grown nearly a meter deeper, down to water that frequent irrigation never pushed them to find.
explanation: Vogt's advice leads you to expect that the frequently watered wheat will do better. The sentence after the blank reports the reverse: the neglected half yielded more. That outcome cuts against the advice, so you need a contrast word, 'However'.

A.why: The root explanation that comes later makes the result feel like a consequence, so you chose a cause word. But the sentence right before the blank only describes how Mendez set up his test. Setting up a test doesn't produce a higher yield. The result matters because it goes against Vogt's advice.

B.why: 'Specifically' introduces a more precise version of what came before. The yield result is a new, unexpected outcome, not a sharper restatement of how Mendez split his fields.

C.why: 'Similarly' signals that the two sentences agree. The result contradicts the advice the passage opens with.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Meteorologists generally look for three ingredients before a tornado: strong wind shear, abundant low-level moisture, and a front or other boundary that forces warm air upward. The tornado that touched down near the farming town of Harlow Creek last April had the first two in abundance. ______, radar and weather-balloon records show no boundary of any kind within 200 kilometers, which leaves forecasters unsure what lifted the air.
explanation: After a list of three ingredients and the news that two were present, you expect to hear that the third was present too. Instead, the next sentence says it was missing. That breaks the expected pattern, so the contrast word 'Yet' is correct.

A.why: The passage counts through the ingredients, so you expected the next sentence to add the third one. It reports that the third ingredient was absent, which goes against the pattern instead of continuing it.

B.why: Having shear and moisture doesn't cause a boundary to be missing. 'Consequently' claims a cause-and-effect link that isn't there.

D.why: 'Namely' would introduce the two ingredients the tornado had. The sentence after the blank is about the missing third ingredient, so it doesn't name those two.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many residents of the Sarno Valley assume that the springs feeding their wells are refilled each year by snowmelt from the peaks directly above town. ______, isotope analysis by hydrologist Mei Tanaka shows that most of the spring water fell as rain on a plateau 60 kilometers to the east and took roughly forty years to seep underground to the valley.
explanation: The first sentence states a common belief, and the second replaces it with what the evidence shows. When a sentence corrects a mistaken assumption with the true fact, 'Actually' is the right transition.

B.why: The residents' belief doesn't cause Tanaka's finding. 'Thus' claims a cause that isn't there and hides the fact that the finding corrects the belief.

C.why: Both sentences are about where the spring water comes from, so they seemed to go together. But they give opposite answers: nearby snowmelt versus distant rain. 'Likewise' signals agreement.

D.why: Tanaka's result isn't an example of the snowmelt belief. It shows the belief is wrong, so 'For instance' gets the relationship wrong.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The oldest flowering-plant fossils known until recently were small, soft-stemmed herbs. As a result, paleobotanists have long pictured the first flowering plants as modest weeds of muddy, frequently disturbed ground. ______, a fossil recently described by paleobotanist Iris Halvorsen is a woody shrub nearly two meters tall, and it is several million years older than any of those herbs.
explanation: The passage builds a picture of the earliest flowering plants as small weeds. Halvorsen's fossil is older than all of those herbs and is a large woody shrub, which overturns that picture. A finding that contradicts the expected view calls for 'However'.

A.why: 'Accordingly' says the fossil fits what came before. A large, older woody shrub goes against the picture of the first flowering plants as small weeds.

B.why: You read the new fossil as one more early flowering plant, an example from the same group. But it doesn't illustrate the small-weed picture. It breaks it.

C.why: 'Moreover' adds a point that supports the one before. The shrub fossil works against the long-held view, so an addition word gets the direction wrong.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The Arctic tern's yearly round trip between the Arctic and Antarctica covers roughly 70,000 kilometers, and it can seem like the most punishing journey any bird undertakes. ______, tracking studies suggest the tern's migration is comparatively gentle. The birds ride prevailing winds for much of the route and feed as they go, whereas the bar-tailed godwit crosses the Pacific in a single nonstop flight of more than 11,000 kilometers without food, water, or rest.
explanation: 'Can seem like' signals an appearance that the passage is about to question. The next sentence says that despite its length, the tern's trip is fairly easy compared with the godwit's. A concession that turns against the first impression fits, so 'That said' is correct.

A.why: 'Indeed' confirms and strengthens the sentence before it. The tracking studies don't confirm that the trip is the most punishing. They suggest it is fairly gentle.

C.why: Both sentences are about how hard the tern's trip is, so you assumed one follows from the other. The trip's length can't be the reason it is gentle. The second sentence goes against the first.

D.why: 'Specifically' introduces a more precise version of the same claim. The sentence after the blank reverses the claim that the trip is the most punishing.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Weathering steel forms a dense outer layer of rust that seals the metal beneath it from moisture. For this reason, engineers have long assumed that bridges built from it can go for decades without protective paint. ______ a recent inspection of a 1970s overpass beside a coastal highway found that salt carried in sea spray had kept that layer from sealing. The overpass's girders were corroding nearly as fast as ordinary unprotected steel.
explanation: The first two sentences set up an expectation: because the rust layer seals the steel, engineers assume these bridges need no paint. The sentence after the blank reports a real case where that layer failed to seal and the steel corroded quickly. That contradicts the assumption, so you need a contrast word. "However" signals that the inspection undercuts what engineers expected.

A.why: You treated the overpass as an example of the engineers' assumption because both sentences are about weathering-steel bridges. An example would have to show the steel lasting without paint. This overpass shows the opposite, so it is a counterexample, not an instance.

B.why: You saw a mechanism described and then an outcome, and you took that as cause and effect. The sealing mechanism did not cause the corrosion. The corrosion happened because the mechanism failed. "As a result" claims a cause the passage never gives, and it skips past the reversal.

D.why: You picked an addition word because both sentences discuss the same bridges and never checked which way the logic runs. Try putting "and also" between them: "engineers assume no paint is needed, and also the steel corroded fast" sounds wrong. The second sentence pushes against the first, so it needs a contrast word.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In a twelve-week trial, nutrition scientist Priya Ramaswamy found that eating two servings of lentils a day lowered participants' LDL cholesterol. It also reduced their fasting blood sugar and made them report feeling fuller after meals. ______ Ramaswamy regards these outcomes as secondary. What interested her most was that participants cut their daily intake of processed meat by nearly a third, even though no one had told them to.
explanation: The first sentences list three impressive health results, and that leads you to expect Ramaswamy to treat them as the main findings. Instead, the next sentence says she sees them as secondary and puts a different, unexpected finding above all of them. That move against the list is a concession: the results are real, but they aren't what matters most to her. "Even so" expresses exactly that.

A.why: You read the passage as a list of good results and assumed the next sentence adds one more. It doesn't add a benefit. It ranks the listed benefits below another finding, and that turns against the list. Because the first sentences are all successes, it's easy to miss that the next one moves in the opposite direction.

B.why: You picked a cause-and-effect word because the sentences follow one another on the same topic. The fact that the health results were strong is not the reason Ramaswamy considers them secondary. If anything, strong results would make you expect her to value them more. "Consequently" claims a cause that isn't there.

C.why: You treated the second sentence as a sharper restatement of the first. "Specifically" would need to zoom in on the same claim, for example by giving exact cholesterol figures. This sentence makes a new and opposing judgment about those results, so it is not a restatement.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Exercise physiologist Ana Ruiz has spent six years refining an altitude-training program for collegiate distance runners, and the measurable gains are impressive: higher red blood cell counts, faster recovery between intervals, and quicker clearance of lactate after hard efforts. Rival coaches who have visited her camp usually ask about those numbers first. ______ the change Ruiz herself values most appears on none of her charts: her runners have become far better at judging their own pace without a watch.
explanation: The passage sets up a list of impressive physiological gains that visitors focus on, so you would expect the next sentence to name one of them as the most important. It doesn't. Instead it pivots against the whole list: the change Ruiz values most is not on her charts at all. That turn against what the earlier sentences lead you to expect needs a concession, and 'That said' signals it.

A.why: You saw the umbrella phrase 'measurable gains' and expected the next sentence to give one of them. But the sentence says the most valued change 'appears on none of her charts', so it is not one of those gains, and it can't be an example of them.

C.why: This is the trap for this kind of question. Every sentence is about the program's benefits, so 'Moreover' sounds like it just adds one more. But the sentence ranks a different change above the whole list of successes. It turns against the list rather than adding to it.

D.why: Neither the gains nor the rival coaches' interest causes Ruiz to value pace judgment most. You chose a cause word because the sentences share a topic, and you never checked whether one actually leads to the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: To make a pipeline coating that repairs its own scratches, materials scientists embedded thousands of microscopic capsules of liquid sealant in an epoxy layer. When a crack ruptures a capsule, the sealant flows out and hardens in the gap. Because each capsule is essentially a tiny void in the epoxy, the team assumed the modified coating would be weaker than ordinary epoxy before any damage occurred. ______ tensile tests showed it was slightly stronger, since the capsules deflected growing cracks.
explanation: The sentence before the blank gives the team's assumption that the capsules would weaken the coating. The sentence after reports what the tests found, which is the reverse: the coating was slightly stronger. When a mistaken belief is followed by the true fact, 'Actually' is the word that marks the correction.

A.why: 'Therefore' would mean the team's reasoning about voids led to the stronger result. The test result overturns that reasoning, so the logic points the other way. You missed the change of direction because both sentences are about the coating's strength.

B.why: 'Similarly' signals that the second sentence matches the first. But the first predicts weakness and the second reports strength. Those two disagree.

D.why: 'Specifically' introduces a more precise version of the same claim. 'Slightly stronger' is not a sharper way of saying 'weaker'. It is the opposite claim.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The fossil leaves at the Kettle Creek site in Montana are small, thick, and coated with a waxy layer, traits that in living plants reduce water loss. For decades, paleobotanists took them as evidence that the region was arid some 60 million years ago. ______ pollen grains and soil chemistry preserved in the same rock layers point to a humid, swampy forest, and the leaves' shape is now thought to reflect nutrient-poor soil rather than drought.
explanation: The first two sentences build up a long-held belief that the site was arid. The sentence after the blank brings in evidence for a humid swamp and reinterprets the leaves. That undercuts the belief rather than supporting it. This is genuine contradiction, so you need 'However'.

A.why: 'Accordingly' would mean the pollen and soil evidence follows from the belief in an arid climate. That evidence actually overturns the belief, so there is no cause and effect here. You picked a result word because the sentences share a topic.

B.why: 'In addition' treats the pollen and soil findings as more support for aridity. They point to a humid swamp instead. Try the 'and also' test: it fails, because the second sentence disagrees with the first.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces a restatement of the same idea. A humid, swampy forest is a different conclusion from an arid one, not a rephrasing of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2021, an advisory panel urged the Harwood County health department to raise its lagging childhood vaccination rate by sending families text-message reminders, a measure the panel praised as cheap and proven in several nearby counties. ______ the department spent its limited budget on home visits by community nurses instead. Its own survey had found that families who missed appointments most often lacked transportation or time off work, problems no reminder could solve.
explanation: The first sentence gives a panel's confident recommendation, so you would expect the department to send text reminders. The next sentence says it did something else. Choosing a different option despite the advice calls for a concession word, and 'Nonetheless' means 'despite that'.

A.why: This is the trap. A recommendation followed by a department decision looks like cause and effect. But the department rejected the advice. The decision happened in spite of the recommendation, not because of it.

C.why: 'Likewise' means the department did something similar to what the panel suggested. Home visits replaced text reminders. They were not a similar measure.

D.why: 'For example' would make home visits one case of the panel's recommendation. The panel recommended text messages, so the nurse visits are not an instance of what it urged.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Linguist Ji-woo Han's team first recorded 200 core words, such as terms for 'water,' 'mother,' and 'eat,' in twelve languages, half with long written traditions and half never written down. They then counted how many of those words each language had replaced over the past century. Because dictionaries and schooling tend to fix a word's form, the team expected the unwritten languages to show far more turnover. ______ the two groups had replaced core words at nearly identical rates.
explanation: The sentence before the blank states what the team expected: much more turnover in the unwritten languages. The sentence after gives the real result: about the same rate in both groups. A mistaken expectation followed by the true finding calls for the correction word 'Actually'.

A.why: You were following the step words 'first' and 'then' and reached for the next one. But the sentence after the blank isn't another step in the procedure. It reports the result, and that result contradicts the team's expectation.

B.why: 'Accordingly' would mean the identical rates follow from the team's reasoning about dictionaries and schooling. That reasoning predicted the opposite outcome, so there is no cause and effect. Both sentences are about turnover, but the logic runs the other way.

D.why: 'Moreover' adds a point that supports the one before it. The finding of identical rates doesn't support the expectation of more turnover. It refutes it.
